name: Task Scheduling Critical Path Method (CPM) Duration Analysis
description: Project managers identify the 'Critical Path'—the longest sequence of dependent tasks that dictates the minimum project completion time.
prompt:
Project managers identify the 'Critical Path'—the longest sequence of dependent tasks that dictates the minimum project completion time.

Execute the required analytical SQL calculation in DuckDB.
Expected output columns: task_code, critical_path_duration, path_str.
Results should be ordered as specified.
setup_sql:
CREATE TABLE project_tasks (
                task_code VARCHAR,
                prerequisite_code VARCHAR,
                duration_days INT
            );
            INSERT INTO project_tasks VALUES
                ('START', NULL, 0),
                ('DESIGN', 'START', 10),
                ('BUILD_FRONTEND', 'DESIGN', 15),
                ('BUILD_BACKEND',  'DESIGN', 25), -- Longest branch
                ('DEPLOY', 'BUILD_BACKEND', 5);
golden_sql:
-- Find the longest path (Critical Path) from START to DEPLOY
            WITH RECURSIVE task_paths AS (
                SELECT 
                    task_code,
                    duration_days AS cumulative_days,
                    task_code AS path_str
                FROM project_tasks
                WHERE prerequisite_code IS NULL
                
                UNION ALL
                
                SELECT 
                    t.task_code,
                    p.cumulative_days + t.duration_days,
                    p.path_str || ' -> ' || t.task_code
                FROM task_paths p
                JOIN project_tasks t ON p.task_code = t.prerequisite_code
            )
            SELECT 
                task_code,
                cumulative_days AS critical_path_duration,
                path_str
            FROM task_paths
            ORDER BY cumulative_days DESC
            LIMIT 1;
why_it_fails: Adding task durations without considering parallel execution branches yields an unrealistically inflated project timeline.
